chunks: From him, from his father, from Hariz, from Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, when Allah, the Exalted, created Adam (peace be upon him), He looked at him and said: 'O Adam.' He said: 'O Lord, what is this?' He said: 'This is a human being I created with My hand and entrusted to you, so prostrate to him.' So they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused, was arrogant, and was of the disbelievers.'

He said: 'I said: O Lord, why did You command me to prostrate to the son of Adam?' He said: 'Because I created him with My hand.' He said: 'I said: O Lord, I will not prostrate to a human being You created from clay.' He said: 'So he went out in haste and anger.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Iblis refuse to prostrate to Adam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this narrative within the Shia doctrine of *Imamah*, framing Adam’s creation as the prototype for the divine vicegerents (*Awliya*) who possess superior spiritual status over the angels. The refusal of Iblis is interpreted not merely as disobedience but as a failure to recognize the *Haqq* (truth) of the Prophet and his progeny, establishing a theological precedent for the hierarchy of creation. This event underscores the test of *Tawhid* through obedience to the designated divine authority, a core theme in Shia exegesis.
